comparison-sorts.title: Insertion sort [3, 1, 2]
comparison-sorts.prompt: The library insertion_sort shifts the prefix with a strict < comparison, so equal keys would not pass each other. This input has no ties.

frames.label: Sorted
frames.narration: insertion_sort returns the sorted list.

cost-models.title: One front pop of three items
cost-models.prompt: list_pop_front_cost_demo(3) returns 2. That is the number of references one pop(0) moves, not a count of three pops.

frames.label: Front pop
frames.narration: One pop(0) on three items moves 2 references.

fast-slow-pointer-patterns.title: Middle, even length, and a cycle entrance
fast-slow-pointer-patterns.prompt: middle_node on 1 through 5 returns 3. On 1 through 4 it returns 3, the second middle. A tail that points at 3 makes find_cycle_start return index 3.

frames.label: Middle
frames.narration: The slow pointer stops on the single middle.

frames.label: Even
frames.narration: The second of the two middles is kept.

frames.label: Entrance
frames.narration: The cycle entrance is the node holding 3.

linked-list-reversal-and-relinking.title: Reverse 1, 2, 3
linked-list-reversal-and-relinking.prompt: reverse_iterative rewrites next links. The list that started as 1, 2, 3 ends as 3, 2, 1.

frames.label: Reversed
frames.narration: The head is now 3.

linked-list-merge-and-sort.title: Merge 1, 4 with 2, 3
linked-list-merge-and-sort.prompt: merge_sorted relinks the existing nodes. The result is 1, 2, 3, 4, and both inputs are left empty.

frames.label: Merged
frames.narration: The heads were compared in order.

linked-list-special-cases.title: Two places from the end of 1, 2, 3, 4
linked-list-special-cases.prompt: nth_from_end counts the tail as 1. A gap of 2 on this list lands on 3.

frames.label: From end
frames.narration: Two steps from the end lands on 3.

doubly-linked-list-operations.title: Unlink a known node
doubly-linked-list-operations.prompt: append a, then b. remove_node on the node for a returns a, and the list that remains is b.

frames.label: Unlink
frames.narration: Removing a known node does not walk the list.

monotonic-stack-patterns.title: Next greater values and a histogram
monotonic-stack-patterns.prompt: next_greater on 2, 1, 2, 4, 3 returns 4, 2, 4, None, None. The histogram area is 10.

frames.label: Answers
frames.narration: next_greater writes the first strictly larger value on the right.

frames.label: Area
frames.narration: The largest rectangle in this histogram has area 10.

stack-parsing-and-expressions.title: Balanced brackets and operator precedence
stack-parsing-and-expressions.prompt: ([]) is balanced and ([)] is not. 2+3*4 becomes 2 3 4 * + and evaluates to 14.

frames.label: Brackets
frames.narration: ([]) is balanced. ([)] crosses pairs and is not.

frames.label: Postfix
frames.narration: Multiplication leaves the operator stack before addition.

noncomparison-sorts.title: Counting sort and digit passes
noncomparison-sorts.prompt: counting_sort of 3, 1, 2, 1 with maximum 3 returns 1, 1, 2, 3. A radix pass keeps equal digits in their old order.

frames.label: Counts
frames.narration: counting_sort places keys by value, not by comparing neighbors.

frames.label: Digits
frames.narration: Least-significant digit passes keep equal-digit order.

order-statistic-selection.title: Quickselect on a small array
order-statistic-selection.prompt: quickselect uses the rightmost value as the pivot. k = 0 returns 1 and k = 2 returns 3 on 3, 1, 4, 2.

frames.label: Smallest
frames.narration: quickselect with k = 0 returns the minimum.

frames.label: Third
frames.narration: k = 2 is the third smallest key, which is 3.

inversion-counting.title: Count pairs that are out of order
inversion-counting.prompt: inversion_count on 3, 1, 4, 2 returns 3. The pairs are (3, 1), (3, 2), and (4, 2).

frames.label: Pairs
frames.narration: Three pairs are out of order in 3, 1, 4, 2.

hash-linear-probing.title: A collision, then a tombstone
hash-linear-probing.prompt: With capacity 4, keys 0 and 4 share a start slot. Deleting 0 leaves a tombstone and lookup of 4 still returns 2.

frames.label: Probe
frames.narration: Key 4 finds slot 0 full and takes the next slot.

frames.label: Tombstone
frames.narration: Deleting 0 leaves a marker so the probe can still reach 4.

lru-cache.title: Evict the least recently used key
lru-cache.prompt: A cache of capacity 2 stores a, then b, uses a, then stores c. b is the key that disappears.

frames.label: Evict
frames.narration: b was the least recent key, so c replaces it.

tree-traversals.title: Preorder and level order of one tree
tree-traversals.prompt: Insert 4, 2, 6, 1. Preorder is 4, 2, 1, 6. Level order is 4, 2, 6, 1.

frames.label: Preorder
frames.narration: Visit the node before either child.

frames.label: Levels
frames.narration: A queue visits each depth before the next.

balanced-search-trees.title: Sorted inserts stay balanced
balanced-search-trees.prompt: Inserting 1, then 2, then 3 into a left-leaning red-black tree leaves 2 at the root. Inorder is still 1, 2, 3.

frames.label: Root
frames.narration: Sorted inserts still leave 2 at the root.

priority-queues.title: Pop the smallest priority
priority-queues.prompt: push 5, then 3, then 4. The first pop returns priority 3 and item b.

frames.label: Pop
frames.narration: The smallest priority leaves first.

graph-representations.title: Count the pairs an adjacency list stores
graph-representations.prompt: A directed graph with vertices A, B, C, D and three edges stores three neighbor pairs. A matrix would store 16 cells.

frames.label: Edges
frames.narration: Three adjacency-list pairs store this graph.

topological-order.title: Kahn's algorithm on a small dag
topological-order.prompt: Edges A to B, A to C, B to D, and C to D produce the order A, B, C, D. A cycle makes topological_order raise ValueError.

frames.label: Order
frames.narration: Kahn's algorithm emits every vertex once.

shortest-paths.title: A longer edge loses to a two-edge path
shortest-paths.prompt: Dijkstra from A reports distance 3 at C, not the direct weight 4. Bellman-Ford allows the negative edge and reports -1.

frames.label: Relax

minimum-spanning-trees.title: Skip the edge that closes a cycle
minimum-spanning-trees.prompt: Undirected edges of weight 1, 2, and 4. Prim and Kruskal both return total weight 3. The weight-4 edge is the one that closes a cycle.

frames.label: Skip
frames.narration: The weight-4 edge closes a cycle and is rejected.

two-pointers.title: Two indexes on a sorted array
two-pointers.prompt: two_sum_sorted on 1, 2, 4, 7 with target 6 returns indexes 1 and 2.
